body.text: Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī
body.translated_text: <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī</s> (The Dhāraṇī of the Form of Omniscience)

body.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Oṃ! Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmiṃ samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma, gṛdhrakūṭe mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśabhir bhikṣuśatair evaṃ pramukhaiś cānekamahāśrāvakādibodhisattvabhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsikopāsikādevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyarājāmātyapaurajānapadaparivāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), together with a great assembly of monks — twelve hundred monks in number — along with numerous great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, monks, nuns, female and male lay-followers, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans and non-humans, kings, ministers, citizens, and countryfolk as retinue.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavāṃś catasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ arcanādisaṃskṛtas tadā bodhisattvaviṣayasandarśanapraṇidhānavyūhasamādhiviṣayadhāraṇīsukhavyūhasamādhānanirdeśacaryāvaiśāradyamahāvaipulyabodhisattvānugatasarvabuddhaparigraha nāma dharmaparyāyasūtrāntaṃ bhāṣitum ārabdhavān / tadā nānāvarṇaraśmayo niścaritāyan prabhābhirayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātun mahatāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: At that time, the Blessed One, surrounded and attended by the four assemblies, honored with worship and the like, began to teach the <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourse) called the <s>Dharmaparyāya</s> (turning of the Dharma) entitled 'The Comprehensive Embrace of All <s>Buddhas</s> Following the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — the Exposition of Conduct, Fearlessness, the Display of the <s>Samādhi</s> of Bliss through <s>Dhāraṇī</s> in the Domain of <s>Samādhi</s>, and the Display of Vows for Showing the Domain of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' Then rays of various colors issued forth, and this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) was filled with a great radiance by this effulgence.

children.text: atha ratnavairocano nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvas taṃ mahānimittaṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā sthāyaikāṃśam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avocat / paramāścaryābhūt tatprāpto 'haṃ bhagavan kuta ime raśmaya āgatāḥ? kasyaiṣa viṣayaprabhāvaḥ? ko 'tra hetupratyayo bhaviṣyati?
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnavairocana</s>, having seen that great portent and miracle, instantly rose, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Most wondrous was what I have witnessed, O Blessed One! From where have these rays come? Whose domain and power is this? What cause and condition will there be for this?'

body.text: bhagavān āha / asti kulaputra pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi, ito buddhakṣetrakoṭīśatasahasragaṅgānadīvālukāsamān buddhakṣetrān atikramya padmā nāma lokadhātu nānāguṇaratnavibhūṣitā nānāratnakūṭāgārādivṛkṣapuṣpakariṇyupaśobhitā / yatraikajātipratibaddhā bodhisattvāḥ padmottaratathāgataḥ sakāśad dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti / tatra lokadhātau indro nāma mahābodhivṛkṣaratnamayāny asti / tasya mūle koṭīśatasahasrasuvarṇapatraratnamayapadmo 'sti / tatrādyarātrau padmottareṇārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ / tatra padmāsananiṣaṇṇā bodhisattvāḥ tasya prātihāryāṇi paśyanti / te sarvalokadhātubhyaḥ āgatā bodhisattvās tāṃ pūjayitvā tatra sthitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'There is, O son of good family, in the south-eastern direction, beyond buddha-fields as numerous as the grains of sand of a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s> <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers from here, a world-system called <s>Padmā</s> (Lotus), adorned with various excellent gems, beautified with various gem-studded mansions, trees, flowers, and ponds. There, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> bound by a single birth [to awakening] hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s> (Supreme Lotus). In that world-system there is a great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree called <s>Indra</s>, made of jewels. At its base there is a lotus made of jewels with a hundred thousand <s>koṭi</s> golden leaves. There, in the first watch of the night, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Padmottara</s>, attained unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening. There the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, seated on lotus seats, behold his miracles. Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have come from all world-systems, having worshipped him, remain there.'

children.text: atha padmottaratathāgatas teṣāṃ āśayānuśayaṃ jñātvā bahujanahitāya sukhāya lokānukampāya devamanuṣyāṇāñ ca hitāya mahāyānasya paripūraṇārtham avaivartikadharmacakraṃ pravartitavān / bodhisattva āha / bhagavan kiyac ciraṃ sā lokadhātuḥ padmottaras tathāgatas tiṣṭhati saddharmaṃ vā / bhagavān āha / bhaviṣyati kulaputra padmottarasya tathāgatasyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ triṃśadantarakalpāni, saddharmaṃ daśāntarakalpāṇ sthāsyati, ye yatra jātā bodhisattvās teṣāṃ catvāriṃśadantarakalpāyuṣpramāṇaṃ / pūrvañ ca kulaputra sā lokadhātuś candanā nāma babhūva / na tv evaṃ pariśuddhā nākīrṇaśuddhasattvā yathaitarhi sā lokadhātuḥ / kulaputra candanāyāṃ lokadhātau candrottamo nāmābhūt tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yāvat sa cāpi viṃśatyantarakalpān dharmaṃ deśayitavān / tasya parinirvāṇakālasamaye cāpy ekatyā bodhisattvāḥ praṇidhānavaśenānyadbuddhakṣetraṃ saṃkrāntāḥ / ye cāvaśiṣṭā bodhisattvānām etad abhavat / adyarātrau madhyame yāme candrottamas tathāgataḥ parinirvāsyati tasya daśāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati / kaḥ saddharmāntardhānasyānantaram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate?
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, knowing the dispositions and latent tendencies of those [beings], for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare of gods and humans, and for the fulfillment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), set in motion the irreversible Wheel of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>avaivartikadharmacakra</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'O Blessed One, how long does that world-system and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s> and the True <s>Dharma</s> endure?' The Blessed One said: 'The lifespan of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, O son of good family, will be thirty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). The True <s>Dharma</s> will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. The lifespan of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> born there will be forty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. Formerly, O son of good family, that world-system was called <s>Candanā</s> (Sandalwood). But it was not as purified or as filled with pure beings as that world-system is now. In the world-system <s>Candanā</s>, O son of good family, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Candrottama</s> (Supreme Moon) [and so forth]. He too taught the <s>Dharma</s> for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And at the time of his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, some <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by the force of their vows, transferred to other buddha-fields. And for the remaining <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, this thought arose: "Tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s> will enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. His True <s>Dharma</s> will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. Who, after the disappearance of the True <s>Dharma</s>, will attain unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening?"'

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena gaganamudro nāma bodhisattvaḥ sa pūrvapraṇidhānena candrottamena tathāgatena vyākṛtaḥ / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputra mama parinirvṛtasya daśāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati; rātryāḥ prathame yāme me saddharmāntarahāsyati, tatraiva rātryāḥ paścime yāme tvam anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase, padmottaro nāma bhaviṣyasi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / tatkāle ye bodhisattvā mahāsattvā yena candrottamas tathāgatas tenopajagmuḥ / upetya te sarve nānāprakārair bodhisattvavikurvaiś candrottamasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam etad avocan / icchāmo vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavann ime daśāntarakalpā nirodham avahitena cittenātināmayituṃ /
children.translated_text: At that time, there was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Gaganamudra</s> who, by his former vow, had been given a prophecy by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>: 'You, O son of good family, after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — the True <s>Dharma</s> will endure for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages). In the first watch of the night my True <s>Dharma</s> will disappear; in the last watch of that very night, you will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). You will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), named <s>Padmottara</s>.' At that time, all the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>. Having approached, they all performed worship of <s>Candrottama</s> with various kinds of <s>Bodhisattva</s> miraculous transformations, and spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'We wish, O Venerable Blessed One, to pass these ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> with our minds absorbed in cessation (<s>nirodha</s>).'

body.text: tatra khalu kulaputra candrottamas tathāgato gaganamudraṃ bodhisattvam āmantryaitad avocat / udgṛhṇa tvaṃ kulaputremaṃ sarvajñātākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ sarvātītānāgatais tathāgataiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair yauvarājyābhiṣiktānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ deśitaṃ / ye caitarhi daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantas tiṣṭhantas te 'pi deśayanti / ye bhaviṣyanty anāgate 'dhvani buddhā bhagavantas te 'pi yauvarājyābhiṣiktabodhisattvānāṃ deśayiṣyanti / tadyathā;
body.translated_text: Thereupon, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> and said: 'Take up, O son of good family, this entrance into the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mystic formula) gateway called the Aspect of Omniscience (<s>Sarvajñatākāra</s>), which has been taught by all past and future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have been consecrated as crown-princes (<s>yauvarājyābhiṣikta</s>). Those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who presently abide in all world-realms in the ten directions — they too teach it. Those who will become <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in the future — they too will teach it to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> consecrated as crown-princes. It is as follows:' —

body.text: jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke saṃmade mahāsaṃmade, devām aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭharkke amimakasi hili cili tili ruruke mahāruruke, jaya durjaye jaye jayamati śānte śāntanirghoṣaṇi, amūlaparichinne, mārasainya vitrāsane, mukte muktapariśuddhe, abhite bhayamocane, bhāra charaṇā dānta vidyāvidyā varuttame, nigrahaṃ parivādināṃ, dharmavādinām anugrahaṃ, ārakṣa dharmavādināṃ caturṇāṃ smṛtyupasthānānām adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadam idaṃ / SjDh_1
body.translated_text: <s>jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke saṃmade mahāsaṃmade, devām aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭharkke amimakasi hili cili tili ruruke mahāruruke, jaya durjaye jaye jayamati śānte śāntanirghoṣaṇi, amūlaparichinne, mārasainya vitrāsane, mukte muktapariśuddhe, abhite bhayamocane, bhāra charaṇā dānta vidyāvidyā varuttame, nigrahaṃ parivādināṃ, dharmavādinām anugrahaṃ, ārakṣa dharmavādināṃ</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadam</s>) that illuminates the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>catuḥ smṛtyupasthāna</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 1]

body.text: buddhakāśaye amama nimama, avevi arthe arthani stīraṇe, lokādhimukte, sandadha paribhāvane, caturṇām āryavaṃśānāṃ, adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadā / SjDh_2
body.translated_text: <s>buddhakāśaye amama nimama, avevi arthe arthani stīraṇe, lokādhimukte, sandadha paribhāvane</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadaprakāśanapadā</s>) that illuminates the four noble lineages (<s>caturṇām āryavaṃśānām</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 2]

body.text: bhāṣithe bhāṣaṇe, dhāre dhārayati, gupte śubhaprabhe tatphale agraphale niṣphale nilaha amukta amukta nirmukte, atravita vimuktavati, vilaphala, ayukta iviti, yiviti ratitula, tulamaṃ ahiṃsāma itivāva, atvānatvāna sarvaloke, aneka livindha abhūsare, hatamatte, veśāgravate, aphala, kaphala, trayāṇām ārakṣitānāṃ adhimuktipadam idaṃ / SjDh_3
body.translated_text: <s>bhāṣithe bhāṣaṇe, dhāre dhārayati, gupte śubhaprabhe tatphale agraphale niṣphale nilaha amukta amukta nirmukte, atravita vimuktavati, vilaphala, ayukta iviti, yiviti ratitula, tulamaṃ ahiṃsāma itivāva, atvānatvāna sarvaloke, aneka livindha abhūsare, hatamatte, veśāgravate, aphala, kaphala</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadam</s>) that illuminates the three things to be guarded (<s>trayāṇām ārakṣitānām</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 3]

body.text: jaḍata, aniharavavatavyo idaṃ phalaṃ, niyāmaphalaṃ, samudānāya vibhūṣa, pasye somantra, anumatto akumatto, chedāvane mantrastā daśabala vigrahasthā, isusthita, sunikhama, tīkṣṇāmati, āloko, atitṛṣṇā, adimati, pratyutpannabuddhapūrvaprahāre, caturṇāṃ samyakprahāṇāṃ, adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_4
body.translated_text: <s>jaḍata, aniharavavatavyo idaṃ phalaṃ, niyāmaphalaṃ, samudānāya vibhūṣa, pasye somantra, anumatto akumatto, chedāvane mantrastā daśabala vigrahasthā, isusthita, sunikhama, tīkṣṇāmati, āloko, atitṛṣṇā, adimati, pratyutpannabuddhapūrvaprahāre</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam</s>) that illuminates the four right exertions (<s>caturṇāṃ samyakprahāṇām</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 4]

body.text: anye manye mane, mamane, vire virate, śame śamitāvi, śānte mukte nirakṣame, same samasame, kṣaye akṣaye, ajiti śānte samiṣṭhe, dhāraṇī ālokāvabhāse, ratnavrate, rasamyavate, jñānavate, meruvate, kṣayanidarśane, lokapradīpanidarśane, caturṇāṃ pratisaṃvidām adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_5
body.translated_text: <s>anye manye mane, mamane, vire virate, śame śamitāvi, śānte mukte nirakṣame, same samasame, kṣaye akṣaye, ajiti śānte samiṣṭhe, dhāraṇī ālokāvabhāse, ratnavrate, rasamyavate, jñānavate, meruvate, kṣayanidarśane, lokapradīpanidarśane</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam</s>) that illuminates the four analytical knowledges (<s>caturṇāṃ pratisaṃvidām</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 5]

body.text: cakṣu ābhāse nidarśane jñānālokanidarśanañ ca, prabhāsane sarvendriya bhūmātikrānte, sarvasava vamāṃ, sarve prāthavā kṣayaṃ kare, gokāha vadane, lokānudarśanavibhū, caturṇāṃ ṛddhipādānām adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_6
body.translated_text: <s>cakṣu ābhāse nidarśane jñānālokanidarśanañ ca, prabhāsane sarvendriya bhūmātikrānte, sarvasava vamāṃ, sarve prāthavā kṣayaṃ kare, gokāha vadane, lokānudarśanavibhū</s> — This is the foundation of aspiration (<s>adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam</s>) that illuminates the four bases of psychic power (<s>caturṇāṃ ṛddhipādānām</s>). [<s>Dhāraṇī</s> 6]

body.text: acale buddhe vṛddhapracale, satva gṛhṇa siddhi, kaṃpati nisiddha smahiṭṭe parekasire, some cande datve acala acala apare vicivale nipale pracacale

children.text: prasare, anaya abhyāse, kaṃkame prabhāvini, drāme nijaso grakkrame nayane indriyāṇāṃ balānām adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_7
children.translated_text: <s>prasare, anaya abhyāse, kaṃkame prabhāvini, drāme nijaso grakkrame nayane</s> — this is the illuminating syllable of the aspiration-stage of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) and <s>balas</s> (powers). / <s>SjDh</s>_7

body.translated_text: <s>acale buddhe vṛddhapracale, satva gṛhṇa siddhi, kaṃpati nisiddha smahiṭṭe parekasire, some cande datve acala acala apare vicivale nipale pracacale</s>

body.text: puṣpe supuṣpe, drumaparihāre, abhayarucire, cekaratke, akṣayam astu, ninire mamale, pañcaśiśire, lokasya vijñāne, nayasaṃgṛhīte ca yukte succhendena saptānāṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_8
body.translated_text: <s>puṣpe supuṣpe, drumaparihāre, abhayarucire, cekaratke, akṣayam astu, ninire mamale, pañcaśiśire, lokasya vijñāne, nayasaṃgṛhīte ca yukte succhendena</s> — this is the illuminating syllable of the aspiration-stage of the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening). / <s>SjDh</s>_8

body.text: cakravajre, maitra samāpade, krānte kete, karuṇa rudīkṣayi, prītirūpe kṣamasaṃpanne, arake varate, kharo khare, amūle mūle, sādhane, caturṇāṃ vaiśāradyānām adhimuktipadaprakāśapadam idaṃ / SjDh_9
body.translated_text: <s>cakravajre, maitra samāpade, krānte kete, karuṇa rudīkṣayi, prītirūpe kṣamasaṃpanne, arake varate, kharo khare, amūle mūle, sādhane</s> — this is the illuminating syllable of the aspiration-stage of the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (kinds of fearlessness). / <s>SjDh</s>_9

body.text: vartte cakre cakradhare varacakre vare pravare, hile hire dhare, ārūpāvate, huhure yathā jibhaṃga niṃvare, yathāparaṃ cariniśe yathā bhayaririśi, satyanirhāre, jaravila, viryanihāra, cūre mārganihāra samādhinihāra prajñānihāra vimuktinirhāra, vimuktijñānadarśananihāra nakṣatranirhāra candranirhāra sūryanirhāra, padāñ caturuttaratathāgatena adbhutaṃ, niradbhutaṃ saṃbuddhaṃ abuddha ihabuddhaṃ, tatrabuddhaṃ nihaṃgamapare, araha daraha paṇḍale

children.text: paṇḍale tatrārtalu, māṃgagharaṇi pūṭani saṃprapūṭani, gatapraṃgamanu niruva, nāśani nāśabandhani, cchicchini, cchicchidrama, yova hiḍiṃgamā vare mare, hanane, bhare bhare bhunde bhire bhire ruṣare, saraṇe, daraṇe, pravartte, calanāḍaye, vidraṃvumā varakhumā, brahmacāriṇa, indravani, dhidhirāyani, maheśvaralalani, mamasume, aramini ekākṣara vivañcani, carasti ābhicandāra sūre, sarvasūrā āvarasūrā, punakanitāṃ, maṇḍitāṃ āyinakaṇḍi jabhāme, gandhare, atra runimakare, bhirohini siddhamatte, vilokamate, buddhādhiṣṭhite, dhāraṇīmukhe, daśānāṃ balānām adhimuktiprakāśanapadam idaṃ // SjDh_10
children.translated_text: <s>paṇḍale tatrārtalu, māṃgagharaṇi pūṭani saṃprapūṭani, gatapraṃgamanu niruva, nāśani nāśabandhani, cchicchini, cchicchidrama, yova hiḍiṃgamā vare mare, hanane, bhare bhare bhunde bhire bhire ruṣare, saraṇe, daraṇe, pravartte, calanāḍaye, vidraṃvumā varakhumā, brahmacāriṇa, indravani, dhidhirāyani, maheśvaralalani, mamasume, aramini ekākṣara vivañcani, carasti ābhicandāra sūre, sarvasūrā āvarasūrā, punakanitāṃ, maṇḍitāṃ āyinakaṇḍi jabhāme, gandhare, atra runimakare, bhirohini siddhamatte, vilokamate, buddhādhiṣṭhite, dhāraṇīmukhe</s> — this is the illuminating syllable of the aspiration-stage of the ten <s>balas</s> (powers [of a Tathāgata]). // <s>SjDh</s>_10

body.translated_text: <s>vartte cakre cakradhare varacakre vare pravare, hile hire dhare, ārūpāvate, huhure yathā jibhaṃga niṃvare, yathāparaṃ cariniśe yathā bhayaririśi, satyanirhāre, jaravila, viryanihāra, cūre mārganihāra samādhinihāra prajñānihāra vimuktinirhāra, vimuktijñānadarśananihāra nakṣatranirhāra candranirhāra sūryanirhāra, padāñ caturuttaratathāgatena adbhutaṃ, niradbhutaṃ saṃbuddhaṃ abuddha ihabuddhaṃ, tatrabuddhaṃ nihaṃgamapare, araha daraha paṇḍale</s>

body.text: samanantarārabdhe khalu punar bhagavatāsmiṃ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśe 'yaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakaṃpitā; tathāvabhāsena daśasu dikṣu sarve lokadhātavaḥ samapāṇītalajātā sphuṭā saṃdṛśyante / ye 'pi teṣv avasthitāḥ samādhidhāraṇīkṣāntipratilabdhā bodhisattvās tathāgatabalena svakasvakeṣu

children.text: buddhakṣetreṣv antarhitā imāṃ sahālokadhātum āgatvā gṛdhrakūṭe bhagavataḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntās tasya pādau śirasā vanditvā nānāprakāraiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tatraiva niṣeduḥ sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśaśravaṇārthaṃ / gaṇanāsamatikrāntāś ca devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍamanuṣyakumbhāṇḍapiśācādayas sannipatitās te tatra padmābuddhakṣetraṃ mahatā bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaṃ tathāgataṃ ca paśyanti / samanantarodāhṛtasyeyaṃ dhāraṇīmukhapraveśasya bhagavatā dvāsaptatibhir gaṅgānadīvālukāsamair bodhisattvair iyaṃ dhāraṇī pratilabdhā daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātusthāṃ buddhān bhagavataś ca guṇavyūhān paśyanti sma / te āścaryaprāptā buddhapūjāṃ kṛtvā samādhibalena tasthuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>-fields, having disappeared, came to this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, approached the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), prostrated at his feet with their heads, performed various kinds of worship, and sat down right there for the purpose of hearing the entrance into the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway of the form of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśa</s>). And beyond all counting, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>manuṣyas</s> (humans), <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), and others assembled there. They beheld the <s>Padma</s> (Lotus) <s>Buddha</s>-field and the <s>Tathāgata</s> surrounded by a great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Immediately after this <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway entrance was uttered by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, seventy-two <s>bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river obtained this <s>dhāraṇī</s> and beheld the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, standing in all world-systems in the ten directions, along with the arrays of their virtues. Having attained wonder and having performed worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, they stood by the power of <s>samādhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Immediately after the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) began this entrance into the <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateway of the form of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatākāra</s>), this tri-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) trembled with six kinds of earthquake; and through that radiance, all world-systems in the ten directions appeared clearly visible, as if on the flat of the hand. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in those [world-systems] who had attained <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), by the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in their respective

body.text: bhagavān āha / imāṃ kulaputra dhāraṇīmukhapraveśaṃ bodhisattvo bhāvayamānaś caturaśītidhāraṇīśatasahasrāṇi dvāsaptatiś ca ṣaṣṭiñ ca sahasrāṇi pratilabhate mahāmaitrīkaruṇādayaḥ / ye ca māṃ dhāraṇīṃ śroṣyanti te 'vaivartino bhaviṣyanti / ye likhiṣyanti te buddhadarśanena saddharmaśravaṇena saṅghopasthānenāvirahitā bhaviṣyanti / ye likhāpayiṣyanti te anuttareṇa parinirvāṇenāvirahitā /

children.text: ye svādhyāyanti teṣāṃ sarvāṇy akarmāni parikṣayaṃ gacchati / ye bhāvayanti teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇy akarmāni naśyuḥ / ye dhārayanti taiḥ pramuditādidaśabhūmīn pratilabhante / ye vācayanti te 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāpsyanti / ye parebhyaś ca vistareṇa bhāṣayanti te tathāgatā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: 'Those who recite it — all their unwholesome <s>karmas</s> come to exhaustion. Those who cultivate it — their five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) karmas are destroyed. Those who retain it — by them the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) beginning with <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) are obtained. Those who teach it — they will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And those who explain it in detail to others — they become <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'O son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who cultivates this entrance to the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-door obtains eighty-four hundred-thousands of <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, and seventy-two and sixty thousand, [endowed with] great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and sympathetic joy (<s>mudita</s>). Those who hear this <s>dhāraṇī</s> will become non-retrogressing (<s>avaivartika</s>). Those who write it down will not be separated from seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, and attending upon the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Those who cause it to be written will not be separated from the supreme <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvam etad avocat / yaiḥ khalu kulaputrātītānāgatapratyutpannais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair asyā dhāraṇyāḥ prabhāvena samyaksaṃbodhiḥ prāptāmaḥ / mayā bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśād imān dhāraṇīṃ prāptā, asyā dhāraṇyāḥ prabhāvena samyaksaṃbodhiḥ prāptā, etarhy api mayā dhāritā vācitā parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśitā / evaṃ khalu maitreya yathā gaganamudrabodhisattvena candrottamatathāgatasya sakāśād imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ prāptā dhāritā vācitā, 'syā dhāraṇyāḥ prabhāvena gaganamudro bodhisattvaḥ candrottamatathāgatasya parinirvāṇād yasyāṃ rātrau prathame yāme saddharmāntarhite tasyāṃ paścime yāme samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāptā padmāyāṃ lokadhātau padmottara nāma tathāgato

children.text: bhavati / tathā kulaputra mama sakāśād iyaṃ drāviḍamantrapadā sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī dhāraya vācaya vistareṇa parebhyaś ca saṃprakāśaya / asyāḥ prabhāvena maitreyāśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ maitreyo nāma tathāgato 'rhaṃ samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati / tena te maitreyaitarhi mamāntikād yauvarājyaṃ parigṛhītaṃ, yathātītānāṃ tathāgatānām antikād atītair bodhisattvair yauvarājyaṃ parigṛhītāḥ //
children.translated_text: — thus, O son of good family, retain, recite, and illuminate in detail for others this <s>Drāviḍa</s>-<s>mantra</s>-word, the <s>Sarvajñatākāra-dhāraṇī</s> (Dhāraṇī of the Form of Omniscience), received from me. By its power, <s>Maitreya</s>, when the lifespan of beings is eighty thousand years, there will arise a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Maitreya</s>. Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, the regency (<s>yauvarājya</s>) has now been received by you from me, just as in the past, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of former times received the regency from former <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.translated_text: Then indeed the Blessed One addressed <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> with these words: 'O son of good family, by the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present have attained perfect awakening. Formerly, O son of good family, I obtained this <s>dhāraṇī</s> from the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and by the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, I attained perfect awakening. Even now I retain it, recite it, and illuminate it in detail for others. Thus indeed, <s>Maitreya</s>, just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s> obtained this <s>dhāraṇī</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, retained it, and recited it — by the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganamudra</s>, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrottama</s>, on that very night, in the first watch when the true <s>Dharma</s> had disappeared, in the last watch, attained perfect awakening in the world-realm called <s>Padmā</s>, becoming a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmottara</s>

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavān sarvāvatīṃ parṣadam avalokya tasyāṃ velāyām imāni mantrapadāny abhāṣata / tadyathā:
body.translated_text: Thereupon, the Blessed One, surveying the entire assembly, at that moment spoke these <s>mantra</s>-words (<s>mantrapadāni</s>). Namely:

body.text: dāntabhūmiḥ damathabhūmiḥ smṛtibhūmiḥ prajñābhūmir vaiśāradyabhūmiḥ pratisaṃvidbhūmir anutkṣepabhūmiḥ samatāparikṣayopekṣabhūmir jātikṣayabhūmir muja vinmujaḥ, malatmajaḥ, visāgraḥ, daśāvate veśataḥ teraṇa, veśalagra, śamuśavataḥ, vimati vimati yopahira regamata vasisakrama iticoravate, makhe mudra daharavate prajñākṣā bubu dahakramitā sadoṣavantaḥ elaya tilaya ahusuṭā amundhamaṃ arthavati, muruvati, tehīnadvivā, akanati bakanate samake visābhaṭe, iṭe iṭabale

children.text: atra tatra kuruṣaṃ laruṣaṃ, latatha katha sarvanta sarvantavaḥ aniruddhaḥ dihakhatambi, phala bahuphala, śataphala, śiṣṭavate, api devānāṃ bhagavāṃ pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyuktāny adhimuktipadāni prakāśayati, eṣu prakāśyamāneṣu ṣaṣṭibhir devanayutaiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam abhūt / SjDh_11
children.translated_text: <s>atra tatra kuruṣaṃ laruṣaṃ, latatha katha sarvanta sarvantavaḥ aniruddhaḥ dihakhatambi, phala bahuphala, śataphala, śiṣṭavate</s> — moreover, the Blessed One illuminates the <s>adhimukti</s>-words (words of aspiration) connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) for the gods. When these were being illuminated, sixty <s>nayutas</s> (myriads) of gods accomplished the vision of truth (<s>satyadarśana</s>).

body.translated_text: <s>Dāntabhūmi</s> (the stage of the tamed), <s>damathabhūmi</s> (the stage of taming), <s>smṛtibhūmi</s> (the stage of mindfulness), <s>prajñābhūmi</s> (the stage of wisdom), <s>vaiśāradyabhūmi</s> (the stage of fearlessness), <s>pratisaṃvidbhūmi</s> (the stage of analytical knowledge), <s>anutkṣepabhūmi</s> (the stage of non-casting-away), <s>samatāparikṣayopekṣabhūmi</s> (the stage of equanimity in the exhaustion of equality), <s>jātikṣayabhūmi</s> (the stage of the destruction of birth) — <s>muja vinmujaḥ, malatmajaḥ, visāgraḥ, daśāvate veśataḥ teraṇa, veśalagra, śamuśavataḥ, vimati vimati yopahira regamata vasisakrama iticoravate, makhe mudra daharavate prajñākṣā bubu dahakramitā sadoṣavantaḥ elaya tilaya ahusuṭā amundhamaṃ arthavati, muruvati, tehīnadvivā, akanati bakanate samake visābhaṭe, iṭe iṭabale</s>

body.text: tatphalam agraphalaṃ, lalaha alaha nilaṃhare, vacatakhyā idaṃphalaṃ, niyāmaphalaṃ, namudaya vibhūkha, prajñācakra, sunirvṛticakra, jñānīcakra, ebhir adhimuktipadair daśānāṃ devakoṭīnāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni tatraivāvaivartikāḥ sthitāḥ / SjDh_12
body.translated_text: <s>tatphalam agraphalaṃ, lalaha alaha nilaṃhare, vacatakhyā idaṃphalaṃ, niyāmaphalaṃ, namudaya vibhūkha, prajñācakra, sunirvṛticakra, jñānīcakra</s> — through these <s>adhimukti</s>-words (words of aspiration), the minds of ten <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of gods were aroused toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and they were established right there in the state of non-retrogression (<s>avaivartika</s>).

body.text: paśya momate, anumate akumato akumati cchīdattake, mantasthā deśabala vipravasthaḥ, iśasthita, atimati tīkṣṇamati, āloko sterituṣṇa, ebhir adhimuktipadaiś catuḥṣaṣṭīnāṃ nāgasahasrāṇāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni, tatraivāvaivartikāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ / SjDh_13
body.translated_text: <s>paśya momate, anumate akumato akumati cchīdattake, mantasthā deśabala vipravasthaḥ, iśasthita, atimati tīkṣṇamati, āloko sterituṣṇa</s> — through these <s>adhimuktipadās</s> (words of resolute faith), sixty-four thousand <s>nāgas</s> had their minds set upon <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment), and right there they became <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing).

body.text: aprabhā samadanā ahadyo bhagavadyo, karaṇyākṣa, siddhamati, samantakṣau, alabale, piṭakaro, mahābale, ojadaro dharaṇe migalakṣa, udākṣa, kukākṣa viroyo, virūpamukha, akṣihasta saṃkṣibala asurodina, asuropramardane, ebhir adhimuktipadair dvādaśānāṃ yakṣakoṭīnāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni tatraivāvaivartikāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ / SjDh_14
body.translated_text: <s>aprabhā samadanā ahadyo bhagavadyo, karaṇyākṣa, siddhamati, samantakṣau, alabale, piṭakaro, mahābale, ojadaro dharaṇe migalakṣa, udākṣa, kukākṣa viroyo, virūpamukha, akṣihasta saṃkṣibala asurodina, asuropramardane</s> — through these <s>adhimuktipadās</s> (words of resolute faith), twelve <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of <s>yakṣas</s> had their minds set upon <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment), and right there they became <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing).

body.text: arthe pilile tinithe, saṃtīthe, katitena nakeme, nanamaste, ubherabhe, mudame, madame, matime, saniha śūre, dhāraṇīye sendra sadeva, sanāga, sayakṣāsuradevā, nāgā nirukti parivāra, niruktarāni, smṛti prajñā parivāramati pratilābhī, gatidhṛtiparivāra gatidhṛtilābhīḥ pūrvakeṣu hiteṣu caritavantaḥ, abhiskāmavantaḥ, śūravantaḥ ciravīryavantaḥ bhītavantaḥ sitabhāge, mārgamudra diśāpakarṣaṇi kṣaparahu, charaṇo devaracatu suramudra, yakṣamudra, rākṣasamudra, vedivedime, tape, tattape uṣṇāname, prakhādya, nanava dhāraṇīya, aviśa diśāśodhane, vākyaśuddhe jihvāśuddhe, vāciparikarmaḥ prajñā buddhi smṛti mati

children.text: gati dhṛti gaṇana pratisaraṇabuddhiḥ, jayacakre śūnyacakre vyaya, ebhir adhimuktipadair ṣaṭpañcāśānām asurasahasrāṇāṃ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni avaivartikāś ca vyavasthitāḥ / SjDh_15
children.translated_text: <s>gati</s> (progress), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), enumeration, resort of intellect, wheel of victory, wheel of emptiness, decay — through these <s>adhimuktipadās</s> (words of resolute faith), fifty-six thousand <s>asuras</s> had their minds set upon <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment), and they became established as <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing).

body.translated_text: <s>arthe pilile tinithe, saṃtīthe, katitena nakeme, nanamaste, ubherabhe, mudame, madame, matime, saniha śūre, dhāraṇīye</s> — together with <s>Indra</s>, together with the <s>devas</s>, together with <s>nāgas</s>, together with <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>devas</s>, [with] the <s>nāgas</s>' linguistic analysis and retinue, linguistic analyses, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), retinue of understanding, attainment of gain, <s>gati</s> (progress) and <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness) as retinue, attainers of progress and steadfastness, having practiced in former beneficial [deeds], possessed of aspiration, possessed of heroism, possessed of long-sustained vigor, possessed of fearlessness, on the white side, the seal of the path, drawing away from the directions, dispelling darkness, going forth, <s>devaracatu suramudra, yakṣamudra, rākṣasamudra, vedivedime, tape, tattape uṣṇāname, prakhādya, nanava dhāraṇīya</s>, purifying the directions, purity of speech, purity of tongue, purification of words, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>mati</s> (understanding),

body.text: tatra bhagavān vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇaṃ bodhisattvam āmantrayate / durlabhaṃ kulaputra tathāgatānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo; durlabhā ime śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaparibhāvitāmī drāviḍamantrapadāḥ; sattvānāṃ hitāya bodhisattvaguṇaniṣpādanārthaṃ kulaputra tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā dānadamasaṃyamakṣāntivīryasamādhiprajñā parigṛhītā bahavo buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāḥ paryupāsitāḥ, kvacid dānan dattaṃ, śīlaṃ rakṣitaṃ, brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ, kvacid bhāvanā niṣevitā, kṣāntir bhāvitā, vīryam ārabdhaṃ, samādhir niṣpāditā, prajñā sevitā, bahvaprameyaṃ vividhanānāprakāraiḥ śubhakarma kṛtaṃ, yenaitarhi mayānuttaraṃ jñānaṃ pratilabdhaṃ / anekāṃ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṃ tathāgatena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāñ caratā, mṛṣāpaiśunyaparuṣasaṃbhinnapralāpā

children.text: varjitā, anekavidhaṃ kuśalaṃ vākkarmaṃ sevitaṃ bahulīkṛtaṃ / yenaitarhi prabhūtajihvā pratilabdhā, na hi kulaputra tathāgatārhatānyathā kathayanti /
children.translated_text: these were abandoned, and manifold wholesome vocal <s>karma</s> was practiced and cultivated abundantly. Through this, the great tongue [of the <s>Tathāgata</s>] was obtained. Indeed, O son of good family, <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Arhats</s> do not speak falsely.

body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇa</s>: 'Rare, O son of good family, is the appearance of <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the world; rare are these <s>Drāviḍa</s> mantra-words perfumed with <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), and <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation). For the benefit of beings and for the accomplishment of <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> formerly, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, cultivated <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), <s>saṃyama</s> (discipline), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. In some [lives] gifts were given, morality was guarded, the holy life was practiced; in some [lives] meditation was cultivated, patience was developed, vigor was aroused, concentration was accomplished, wisdom was practiced — manifold and immeasurable, of various kinds, wholesome <s>karma</s> was performed, by which I have now obtained the supreme knowledge. For innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> formerly, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, [abandoned] falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and idle talk —

body.text: atha bhagavān tatrarddhyabhisaṃskāram akārṣīt / tenarddhyabhisaṃskāreṇa sarvapuṇyasamavasaraṇaṃ samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / mukhāc ca jihvendriyaṃ nirṇāmayitvā svaṃ mukhaṃ pracchādya tasmāj jihvendriyāt ṣaṣṭiraśmikoṭyo pramuktās taiś cāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātur udāreṇāvabhāsena nirayatiryagyoniyamalokadevamanuṣyāḥ sphuṭā babhūvuḥ / te ca raśmayo ye nairayikāḥ sattvā agninā prajvalitagātrā dahyante teṣāṃ śītalā vāyavo vānti, yeṣāṃ spṛṣṭānāṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ sukhā vedanā prādurbabhūva / ekaikasya ca nairayikasya purataḥ buddhanirmitaṃ tiṣṭhati dvātriṃśadbhir lakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛta aśītibhiś ca, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā te nairayaikāḥ sukhasamarpitā buddhadarśanāpyāyitaśarīrā buddhaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ cintayanto, 'sya sattvasyānubhāvenāsmābhiḥ sukhā vedanā pratilabdhās; te bhagavataḥ sakāśe premāprasādagauravaṃ saṃjanayanti /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One performed a miraculous feat of supernatural power there. By that miraculous feat, he entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called 'The Gathering of All Merit.' And extending his tongue from his mouth, covering his own face, from that tongue sixty <s>koṭi</s> (ten millions) of rays were released. By these rays, this billion-world system (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) was filled with a great radiance — the hell-beings, those born in the animal realm, the realm of <s>Yama</s>, gods, and humans were all illuminated. Those rays [reached] those hell-beings whose bodies were ablaze and burning with fire — upon them cool winds blew, and when touched by them, a pleasant sensation arose in that very instant. Before each hell-being appeared a Buddha-emanation (<s>buddhanirmita</s>), adorned with the thirty-two [major] marks and the eighty [minor marks]. Seeing him, those hell-beings, endowed with happiness, their bodies refreshed by the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>, seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, thought thus: 'Through the power of this being, we have obtained pleasant sensation.' They generated love, serene faith, and reverence toward the Blessed One.

children.text: buddhanirmita āha / bhoḥ sattvā evaṃ bhāṣadhvaṃ, namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāya, nityam evaṃ sukhasamarpitā bhaviṣyatha / tatas te nairayikās sattvā añjaliṃ pragṛhya vācam udīrayanti, namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāya / atha te sattvās tena cittaprasādakuśalamūlena tataś cyavitvā ekatyā deveṣūpapannā ekatyā manuṣyeṣu, tathaiva pūrvavad yāvat / ye śītanārakāṃ sattvāḥ pretāḥ piśācā vā sukhasamarpitā devamanuṣyeṣūpapannā evaṃ devamanuṣyatiryakṣu lokeṣu raśmayas saṃcodanti /
children.translated_text: The Buddha-emanation said: 'O beings, speak thus: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>! And you shall always be endowed with happiness.' Then those hell-beings, extending their joined palms, uttered the words: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>!' Then those beings, by that root of merit consisting of faith in the mind (<s>cittaprasādakuśalamūla</s>), passing away from there, some were reborn among the gods and some among humans, and so on as before. Those beings in the cold hells, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and <s>piśācas</s> (demons), endowed with happiness, were reborn among gods and humans. Thus in the worlds of gods, humans, and animals the rays urged them on.

body.text: gaṇanātikrāntā devamanuṣyā bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya niṣaṇṇā karuṇāpuṇḍarīka nāma mahāyānasūtradharmaśravaṇāya / tena ca samayena gaṇanātikrāntā devamanuṣyakāyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayām āsuḥ / gaṇanātikrāntāś cātra bodhisattvāḥ samādhikṣāntidhāraṇīḥ pratilabdhavantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Innumerable gods and humans approached the Blessed One, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, and sat down to hear the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) <s>sūtra</s>-dharma called <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka</s> (White Lotus of Compassion). At that time, innumerable assemblies of gods and humans generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And innumerable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> here attained <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mystic formulas).

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanā sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. That entire assembly, delighted, along with the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī</s> from the Noble and Glorious <s>Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Mahāyāna Sūtra</s>.
